questions.section: PART ONE: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS (20 marks) - Comprehension (the cover lists Part one as Comprehension questions)
questions.question:
Read the passage below then answer the questions that follow

Pollution is the degradation of natural environment by external substances introduced directly or indirectly. Human health, ecosystem quality, aquatic and terrestrial biodiversity may be affected and altered permanently by pollution.

Pollution occurs when ecosystems cannot get rid of substances introduced into the environment. The critical threshold of its ability to naturally eliminate substances is compromised and the balance of the ecosystem is broken.

The sources of pollution are numerous. The identification of these different pollutants and their effects on ecosystems is complex. They can come from natural disasters as the result of human activity, such as oil spills, chemical spills and nuclear accidents.

These can have terrible consequences on people and the planet where they live: destruction of the biodiversity, increased mortality of the human and animal species, destruction of natural habitat, damage caused to the quality of soil, water and air.

Preventing pollution and protecting the environment necessitate the application of the principles of sustainable development. we have to consider to satisfy the needs of today without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs. This means that we should remedy existing pollution, but also anticipate and prevent future pollution sources in order to protect the environment and public health.

Any environmental damage must be punishable by law, and polluters should pay compensation for the damage caused to the environment.

Answer the following the questions fully (20 marks)

1. What is meant by pollution?
questions.answer_guide: Pollution is the degradation (damage) of the natural environment by external substances that are introduced into it directly or indirectly.

questions.section: PART THREE: GRAMMAR IN USE (30 MARKS) - A
questions.question:
A) Change the verbs in brackets into past perfect tense to complete the sentences (10 marks)
   1. The visitors ........................ (walk) for such a long Distance.
   2. They ........................ (do) their final exams.
   3. My Brother ........................ (write) a beautiful poem.
   4. Hodan ........................ (live) in Mogadishu by the time I met her.
   5. They ........................ (fly) to many countries before their father was posted to Somalia.
questions.answer_guide:
1. had walked
   2. had done
   3. had written
   4. had lived
   5. had flown

questions.section: PART THREE: GRAMMAR IN USE (30 MARKS) - B
questions.question:
B) Put the verbs in brackets into the correct tense (10 marks)
   1. If she ........................ (take) salt at night, something bad will happen to her.
   2. If Hodan ........................ (go) to the library, she will bring me a novel.
   3. If I ........................ (be) you, I would work extremely hard this year.
   4. I ........................ (be) very happy if I had twenty million dollars.
   5. He would have got the job if he ........................ (not be) so nervous in the interview.
questions.answer_guide:
1. takes (first conditional: if + present simple, will + verb)
   2. goes
   3. were (second conditional: if + past simple, would + verb)
   4. would be
   5. hadn't been (third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle)

questions.section: PART THREE: GRAMMAR IN USE (30 MARKS) - C
questions.question:

   3. The man ate all the food. (past perfect)
   4. The club collected a lot of money during the fundraiser. (simple future)
   5. Mahad wrote an official letter to the journalism club. (present continuous)

   2. Amal has been running well since the whistle blew.
   3. The man had eaten all the food.
   4. The club will collect a lot of money during the fundraiser.

questions.section: PART FOUR: LITERATURE (15 MARKS) - Answer the following questions (7 marks)
questions.question:
Answer the following questions (7 marks)

1. What are the features of oral literature? (3 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
Any three features of oral literature:
   1. It is passed on by word of mouth (spoken, not written) from one generation to the next
   2. It is performed before an audience, who often take part (singing, clapping, responding)
   3. It is communal and usually has no known author, uses repetition, songs, gestures and changes as it is retold; it also preserves the culture and values of a society

questions.section: PART FOUR: LITERATURE (15 MARKS) - Answer the following questions (7 marks)
questions.question: 2. Define a myth. (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide: A myth is a traditional story, often about gods, heroes or supernatural beings, that explains the origin of the world, people, or natural events and beliefs of a community.

questions.section: PART FOUR: LITERATURE (15 MARKS) - Answer the following questions (7 marks)
questions.question: 3. Define satirical poetry. (2 mark)
questions.answer_guide: Satirical poetry is poetry that uses humour, irony, ridicule or exaggeration to criticise and expose the weaknesses, faults or wrongs of people, leaders or society, often to bring about change.

questions.section: PART FOUR: LITERATURE (15 MARKS) - Poem (8 marks)
questions.question:
Read the following poem and answer the questions (8 marks)

NIGHTFALL IN SOWETO

[The poem is printed in full on page 8 of the paper. Its text is not reproduced in this file because it is a published, copyrighted poem; insert it from the official paper if the full text is needed.]

Answer these questions
   1. What is the poem about?
   2. Who is the persona in this poem?
   3. What is the tone of the poem?
   4. What is the mood of the poem?
questions.answer_guide:
(Answers are in my own words, based on the poem as printed in the paper; each question is worth 2 marks.)

   1. The poem is about the fear and insecurity of township residents in Soweto, who feel hunted every night and have no safe place, so they long for daytime to last forever.
   2. The persona is an ordinary black resident of Soweto, a helpless victim living in terror of the violence that comes with nightfall.
   3. The tone is fearful, desperate and bitter / resentful (the persona is pleading and complaining).
   4. The mood is tense, frightening and gloomy (it makes the reader feel the persona's terror and helplessness).

questions.section: PART FIVE: COMPOSITION WRITING (15 MARKS)
questions.question:
Choose one of the two topics given below, and write composition not less than 150 words

Topic 1:
Write a composition about the importance of water, explaining each point of the following points. If you left one of the given points you will totally lose your marks. Your composition should not less than 150 words
   1. Where do we find the water?
   2. Why the water is very important to our lives?
   3. Why do the animals and plants need water?
   4. What will happen if we don't get water?

OR

Topic 2:
Write a composition about the exported products in Puntland
questions.answer_guide:
Topic 1 (importance of water): a good composition of at least 150 words with an introduction, one paragraph for each of the four points, and a conclusion:
   1. Where we find water: rain, rivers, lakes, seas and oceans, underground (wells and boreholes), springs, ice
   2. Importance to our lives: drinking, cooking, washing and hygiene, farming and irrigation, industry and electricity, transport
   3. Animals and plants: plants need water for photosynthesis, growth and to carry nutrients; animals need it for drinking, digestion and regulating body temperature, and many live in water
   4. If we don't get water: thirst, dehydration, disease, death of crops and animals, famine, drought and conflict

Topic 2 (exported products of Puntland): a composition of at least 150 words with an introduction, a paragraph on each main product, and a conclusion. Main points: livestock (goats, sheep, camels, cattle) exported through Bosaso and other ports; frankincense and myrrh; fish and other marine products; hides and skins; gum and resins. Explain where they come from, where they are sold (e.g. the Gulf states), how they bring income and jobs, and challenges and suggestions (quality, ports, security).
